title: Madhuri Dixit, Triptii Dimri, and a Dead Body in the Kitchen. Netflix's Maa Behen Drops June 4.
excerpt: Suresh Triveni's dark comedy about a mother and her two daughters covering up a crime features a Dhak Dhak Reloaded and Ravi Kishan at his chaotic best.
body:
There's a dead body in the kitchen. The mother and her two daughters don't agree on anything except that they need to make it disappear. Welcome to *Maa Behen*, Netflix's next Hindi original, arriving June 4.

## The Setup

Directed by Suresh Triveni — the filmmaker behind *Tumhari Sulu* and *Jalsa* — *Maa Behen* stars Madhuri Dixit as Rekha, Triptii Dimri as Jaya, and content creator Dharna Durga (making her film debut) as Sushma. Ravi Kishan plays Gupta Ji in what's being described as a scene-stealing supporting role. The cast also includes Geetanjali Kulkarni, Arunoday Singh, Jatin Sarna, and Shardul Bhardwaj.

The story is set in Adarsh Colony, a conservative neighbourhood where the three women are already the subject of scrutiny. When they discover a corpse in their kitchen, the perpetually bickering trio is forced into an unlikely collaboration — turning their familial dysfunction into a survival strategy while dealing with nosy neighbours, family drama, and a chain of increasingly chaotic situations.

## Darkly Funny, Deliberately Uncomfortable

The film operates in the same tonal space as *Darlings* (2022) — Netflix's Alia Bhatt-Shefali Shah hit that mixed domestic tension with dark humour and crime. Triveni, who has consistently shown an ability to fuse drama with emotional precision, seems to be pushing further into genre territory here. The trailer promises loud humour, emotional turns, and a visual energy that's designed for the OTT format.

The soundtrack features a *Dhak Dhak Reloaded* — yes, that *Dhak Dhak* — reworked by Akshay and IP from the 1992 Anand-Milind original. For diaspora audiences who grew up watching Madhuri's iconic *Beta* performance, hearing that beat in a completely different context is going to be a moment.

## Madhuri's Streaming Evolution

For Madhuri Dixit, *Maa Behen* continues a deliberate pivot that started with *The Fame Game* on Netflix. After three decades as one of Hindi cinema's most recognizable faces, she's choosing roles that are character-driven, morally ambiguous, and far removed from the song-and-dance framework that defined her peak years. Playing a mother covering up a crime with her daughters is about as far from *Hum Aapke Hain Koun* as you can get — and that's exactly the point.

Triptii Dimri, meanwhile, is on a trajectory that seems to have no ceiling. From *Bulbbul* to *Qala* to *Animal* to *Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3*, she's built a filmography that toggles between critical acclaim and massive commercial success. Pairing her with Madhuri for the second time (after *Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3*) gives the film a generational dynamic that's built into the casting itself.

## For the Diaspora

Produced by Vikram Malhotra's Abundantia Entertainment and Triveni's Opening Image Films, *Maa Behen* premieres globally on Netflix on June 4. The promotional campaign has already gone viral — a flash mob at a Gurugram mall featured the three leads arriving on a decorated rickshaw, complete with a "Roti Challenge" that had the crowd in splits.

If you're looking for the kind of Hindi film that your whole family can argue about afterwards — some will call it a masterpiece, others will say it's too loud, everyone will remember the punchlines — mark June 4.
author: Diaspora Desk
